introduce.title: This is not another pile of links
introduce.label: How WebTools helps
introduce.description: The hard part is not finding more tools. It is knowing what to do now, why a tool fits, and what evidence means you are ready to move on. WebTools turns scattered information into a next step you can judge and execute.

items.title: Browse resources across seven stages
items.description: Locate your current stage, from demand discovery to operating and growth, then filter for tools relevant to that task.

items.title: Follow action guides built around an outcome
items.description: Each guide tells you what to do first, what evidence to keep, and when you are ready for the next step.

items.title: See practical use, not just a summary
items.description: Resource entries explain the problem a tool solves, how to start using it, and what to check before choosing it.

items.title: Keep asking with your project context
items.description: After signing in, keep questions, files, and project progress in one workspace and see which site sources informed each answer.

benefits.title: Use the right entry point for the problem you have
benefits.label: Where to start
benefits.description: You do not need to read the whole site. First decide whether you need one tool, a complete execution path, or advice grounded in your own project.

items.title: You know the task, but not which tool to use
items.description: Open the resource library and filter by demand discovery, idea validation, prototyping, building, launch, optimization, or growth.

items.title: You have a goal, but not a concrete first step
items.description: Open an action guide, complete the steps, and keep reusable outputs such as user quotes, the riskiest assumption, or the core product flow.

items.title: Your question depends on your project context
items.description: Sign in to the AI workspace and connect the conversation to a project. It can combine site knowledge, optional web search, files, and project memory.

usage.title: Get the three earliest product decisions right
usage.description: The first action guides cover the path from problem discovery to a testable prototype. Each step leaves a concrete output, so progress is not based on guesswork.

items.title: Find a problem worth validating
items.description: Collect recurring problems from real discussions and existing products, leaving at least ten user quotes with context.

items.title: Validate whether the idea has demand
items.description: Check alternatives, traffic, and revenue signals. Write down the riskiest assumption and disconfirming condition before deciding to continue, adjust, or stop.

items.title: Build something users can test
items.description: Implement only the critical user path, define the screen order, and let target users understand, click, and expose problems.

items.title: Continue through the remaining stages
items.description: Once the evidence holds, return to the resource library for development, databases, payments, deployment, analytics, SEO, and growth tools.

features.title: Every resource must answer a real selection question
features.description: This is not a bulk directory. Each entry is organized around a real task, so you know whether a tool is worth opening before you reach its homepage.

items.title: What it is

items.title: What problem it solves

items.title: When to use it
items.description: Stage and trigger conditions help you avoid adopting tools before they are needed.

items.title: How to get started
items.description: A concrete first move lets you act without starting the research again from scratch.

items.title: What to check before choosing
items.description: Pricing, capability limits, maintenance status, and other risks are called out when relevant.

items.title: Where to go next
items.description: Related stages, categories, and action guides reconnect a single tool to the full product journey.

faq.title: A few things to confirm before you begin
faq.description: Public content is ready to browse. Use the AI workspace when you need ongoing support for a specific project.

items.title: I already use AI coding tools. Is WebTools still for me?
items.description: Yes. WebTools is primarily for people who can use AI coding tools but have not yet completed the full path from demand validation and design to development, launch, and growth on their own.

items.title: How do I get started?
items.description: If you know the task, browse resources by stage. If you do not know the steps, start with an action guide. If the answer depends on your project, sign in to the AI workspace.

items.title: Do resources and action guides require sign-in or payment?
items.description: No. The homepage, resource library, action guides, articles, and about page are public. AI conversations, project memory, and file uploads require sign-in and use Credits.

items.title: What information can the AI assistant use?
items.description: The site knowledge base is retrieved automatically. Web search and Skills are used only when you enable them. Answers can also use project memory and uploaded files, with the actual sources shown.

cta.title: Do not collect more tools. Finish the next step.
cta.description: If you know the task, find resources by stage. If you do not know how to proceed, choose an action guide and start executing.
